recommendations.rewrite: "We cut month-end close from 9 days to 3." Priya Shah, Finance Director, Northwind Logistics

recommendations.issue: Competence and judgement scores 1 of 4. Replace what you were responsible for with what changed because of you: action verb, what you did, measurable result.
recommendations.original: Responsible for managing the engineering team.
recommendations.rewrite: Grew the engineering team from 6 to 25 and cut release time from monthly to daily.

recommendations.issue: Stakes: pain and desire scores 0 of 4. Describe the specific moment the reader realises the current way is not working, in their words.
recommendations.rewrite: It is 11pm on the last day of the quarter and you are still matching receipts to bank lines.

recommendations.issue: Surprise, humour and delight scores 1 of 4. Include one thing the reader would not predict: a counter-intuitive fact, a reversal, a reframe. Then pay it off.
recommendations.original: Most teams want to ship faster.
recommendations.rewrite: The fastest teams we studied ship less code, not more. Here's why.

recommendations.issue: Concreteness and vividness scores 2 of 4. Swap each abstract noun for something the reader can picture: a person, a moment, an object, a number.
recommendations.original: We deliver holistic, seamless solutions that empower teams.
recommendations.rewrite: Your team sees every open ticket on one screen, so nobody chases updates in Slack.

recommendations.issue: Objection handling scores 0 of 4. Name the sceptic's strongest objection and answer it with evidence. Two-sided beats one-sided for sceptical readers.
recommendations.rewrite: Yes, we cost more than a freelancer. You are paying for a team that does not disappear in August.

recommendations.issue: Specific claims and evidence scores 1 of 4. Replace every 'improved', 'faster', 'more' with a number, a time frame and a baseline.
recommendations.rewrite: Cut page load from 4.1s to 1.3s in six weeks.

recommendations.issue: Structure and flow scores 2 of 4. Put the main claim or outcome in the first line. Build the case after.
recommendations.original: Founded in 2010, we have worked across many sectors... (point in paragraph 4)
recommendations.rewrite: We cut onboarding time in half for B2B SaaS teams. Here is how.

recommendations.issue: Cost of delay scores 0 of 4. Show what staying put costs per week, month or year, using the reader's numbers where possible.
recommendations.original: Don't wait to fix your hiring process.
recommendations.rewrite: Each month a senior role stays open costs roughly [£X] in delayed delivery.

recommendations.issue: The call to act scores 2 of 4. End with a single, specific, low-friction action and say what happens when the reader takes it.
recommendations.original: Let us know if you have any questions.
recommendations.rewrite: Reply 'yes' and I will send two times for a 20-minute call next week.

recommendations.issue: Mythos scores 0 of 4. Frame the message inside a bigger narrative: an old world, a shift, winners and losers, a promised land.
recommendations.rewrite: Buyers now do 70% of their research before talking to sales. The teams winning have stopped pitching and started teaching.

recommendations.issue: Dialogue scores 0 of 4. End with a genuine question or an invitation to challenge the argument. It signals confidence and respect, and turns a pitch into a conversation.
recommendations.original: Because our customers have told us, clearly, that they want one person to call rather than five.
recommendations.rewrite: That's how we see it. Where do you think it breaks down for your team?

recommendations.issue: Structure scores 2 of 4. Put the main point or ask in the first two sentences, then order the rest as reasons, proof, next step.
recommendations.original: We have been operating since 2010 and offer many services... (ask in the final paragraph)
recommendations.rewrite: We can halve your onboarding time. Here's how, and what it would take.

recommendations.issue: Length scores 2 of 4. Cut anything that doesn't serve the one big idea; aim for the usual range for this content type.
recommendations.rewrite: (The same email at 120 words, with one ask)

recommendations.issue: First impression scores 2 of 4. Open with the reader's situation, a specific fact or the big idea; cut greetings-as-content and background.
recommendations.original: I hope this email finds you well. My name is Tom and I work at BrightPath.
recommendations.rewrite: Your Q3 update mentioned the cloud migration twice.

recommendations.issue: Explicit or implicit scores 1 of 4. Explicit: say it plainly, summarise, repeat the point. Implicit: suggest more than you state; trust shared understanding.
Brief or detailed scores 2 of 4. Brief: headline and essentials; detail on request. Detailed: process, specifics, guarantees and risk mitigation up front.

Team,

Over the next two years we are going to change how we serve our customers. This is a long-term journey, and we will make it together.

Why? Because our customers have told us, clearly, that they want one person to call rather than five. That is the reason for the new account teams.

Nothing changes for you this month. In June each of us will join an account team, and your manager will talk to you personally before then.

I know change is hard. I also know this team, and I trust us to build something lasting for our community.

Priya
